name: Japandi

influenced_by: Scandinavian minimalism — the name is a portmanteau of the two

places: a Western design-media invention rather than a lived place; draws on both Japanese and Scandinavian design history
garments: not a fashion look — an interior-design style
reacts_against: cluttered maximalism, combining Japanese restraint and Scandinavian warmth into one pared-back, natural-material palette.

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Natural materials, wood, bamboo, asymmetry, imperfection
wiki_facts.key_colours: White, grey, green, beige, brown, muted blue
wiki_facts.key_values: Hygge and Wabi-Sabi philosophy, functionality, simplicity, sustainability

findings: mostly muted — about 87% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
